background_notes.justification: A finite Fourier projection converges in Lp time. Taking a subsequence, its coefficients converge almost everywhere; a diagonal choice handles the countably many modes. Pass the uniform squared bound to each finite weighted coefficient sum and then take the supremum over increasing finite projections. This proves the bound almost everywhere.
